parts.label: a
parts.text:
Sketch the curve with equation $y = -x(x + 4)(x + 3)$

Show the coordinates of the points where the curve meets the coordinate axes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the set of values of $x$ for which $-x(x + 4)(x + 3) > 0$

rows.answer: Correct cubic shape with negative $x^3$ coefficient
Crosses the $x$-axis at three distinct points
Uses their sketch to identify where the curve is above the $x$-axis

answer.method: sympy (exact symbolic solution, numeric values evaluated from the exact form)

parts.label: a
parts.text:

Show clearly the equations of the asymptotes and the coordinates of the points where $C$ crosses the coordinate axes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your sketch to explain why the equation $\dfrac{- 2 x - 1}{x - 4} = -4$ has exactly one solution, and find it.

rows.answer: Correct shape: two branches in opposite quadrants of the asymptotes
The horizontal line $y = -4$ meets $C$ once (it is not the asymptote)

answer.method: sympy (exact symbolic solution, numeric values evaluated from the exact form)

rows.answer: Rearranges $2 x^{3} - 4 x - 2 = 0$ so that one side is $x^3 - 4x + 1$

answer.method: sympy (exact symbolic solution, numeric values evaluated from the exact form)
